title: Predatory Charging and Cancellation
body:
I have truly never given anything a one star review before! This is crazy! 

This app intentionally targets people with attention deficit issues, markets itself as self improvement, provides limited and rather mundane material. It breaks cancellations into two innocuous components, so even if the user thinks they’ve cancelled (and receives a cancellation email) they will continue charging exorbitant fees on a monthly basis. Additionally, once you’ve started the cancellation process, you can no longer log onto the app to continue it — meaning it’s even harder to complete cancellation without literally reaching out to customer support. Additionally, mystery purchases have appeared on my account from the period AFTER I had cancelled and lost the ability to log in. This is such a scam! I recommend suspension from the App Store until they fix their subscription issues.
author: Zoeeee D

title: NOT FOR ADHD Be prepared for a money grab
body: I was influenced through social media advertising to try the Wisey app, thinking it would be a good help for my ADHD to focus.  In true ADHD Fashion, I didn’t have time to fully download and get it set up at the time I purchased my trial.  When I thought about it again, a few weeks later, I went back and tried name of the app was and couldn’t find it. Today I found the ONE SINGLE EMAIL they sent confirming my purchase with no actual link provided to what was not an app. It was a website-which I only found after emailing Support and requesting a refund for the $70 subscription charge. I realized I had also been billed. If you have actual ADHD, you understand why one singular email with no working links is a complete and total waste. They don’t actually want to help you, they want you to forget that you ever purchase this and continue billing you.
author: bdittyisme

title: THE TRIAL IS A TRAP
body:
I strongly advise staying far away from the Wisey app. What looks like a harmless trial quickly turns into a non-refundable $99 charge, and by the time you realize it, you’re already stuck.

When I reached out to customer service for a refund, it turned into a frustrating, high-pressure exchange. Instead of helping, they repeatedly tried to keep me on the hook and even attempted to upsell me on a $5 “lifetime subscription”—which makes absolutely no sense given the $99 charge they’re refusing to reverse. It felt less like support and more like a scripted sales funnel designed to extract even more money.

The most concerning part is that they appear to bypass the normal subscription protections you’d expect through Apple’s App Store. That means you don’t get the usual transparency or easy cancellation process, and their strict no-refund policy is buried in the fine print until it’s too late.

In my opinion, this is a predatory setup. I’ve had a terrible experience and will be disputing the charge with my bank. I’ll also be warning others about Koflimin Limited and the operation behind Wisey.

Buyer beware—this one’s not worth the headache.

After the initial rude email, I got the run around and then finally they stopped responding to my very polite request to have the $30 bucks I paid to sign up refunded.
